chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If a man marries off (his daughter) but his father refuses that, then the marriage of the father is valid, even if the grandfather dislikes it. This is not like what the grandfather does, then the father wants to reject it.
ai.seo_question: Who has the primary authority to marry off a daughter if the father and grandfather disagree?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the hierarchy of marital authority (wilayah) within the Shia fiqh, establishing the father's precedence over the grandfather in arranging a daughter's marriage. It highlights a key jurisprudential distinction: while the father's decision stands even if the grandfather objects, the reverse is not true, emphasizing the father's primary role in the family structure as derived from the Prophet's tradition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If the man gets (his daughter) married, but his father refuses that, so the marriage of the father is allowed, even if the grand-father dislikes it. This is not like which the grand-father does, then the father wants to reject it’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Dawud ibn al- Husayn from al-‘Abbas who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If a man marries, then his father rejects it, giving in marriage by the father is permissible; if the grandfather dislikes it, it is not like the case where grandfather gives in marriage, then father wants to reverse it.”’
